headline: US stocks ended mixed as Brent crude neared $106 on renewed Russia-Ukraine strikes and Middle East tensions ahead of major bank earnings and CPI data
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) rose 0.3% to 51,817 while the S&P 500 ($SPX) slipped 0.1% to 7,802 and the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) fell 0.4% to 27,245 as money rotated from technology into value and energy shares.
- Brent crude (@QA) climbed to roughly $106 per barrel after Russia launched fresh strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities just hours after President Trump’s announced Russia‑Ukraine “energy ceasefire” and diesel‑supply deal and following weekend Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia.
- Nine of 11 S&P 500 ($SPX) sectors advanced, led by energy, with ExxonMobil (XOM) and ConocoPhillips (COP) each gaining more than 1.5%.
- Technology underperformed as Nvidia (NVDA) fell on competitive pressure from Microsoft’s in-house AI chip plans and Micron Technology (MU) declined amid China’s CXMT advancing next-generation DRAM production, while Lumentum Holdings (LITE) and Ciena (CIEN) dropped with no clear company-specific catalyst and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell over 2%.
- Salesforce (CRM) climbed after BofA (BAC) Global Research upgraded the shares to buy from underperform.
- Meta Platforms (META) advanced within the communication services sector on enthusiasm for its new Wonder AI models.
- eBay (EBAY) gained, trading up about 3.5% earlier in the session, after being named a top analyst pick and receiving an analyst upgrade.
- FIGS (FIGS) jumped more than 12%.
- Bloom Energy (BE) slid over 6% after the company set the date for its earnings release.
- The U.S. bond market was closed for Columbus Day as equity traders prepared for Tuesday’s bank earnings from JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS), Wells Fargo (WFC) and Citigroup (C) and Wednesday’s CPI inflation report, while Goldman Sachs upgraded global equities on earnings optimism.
